title: Training Notes — Payment Standing and the Independent Living Annual Increase Ceiling
content:
The contract ceiling percentage of an annual increase of the Independent Living Residency Agreement monthly service fee is also reduced for payment standing.

**Rule.** Payment standing is counted as the returned payments posted on the residency within the 12 months ending on the day the increase is recorded. A residency with no returned payment has the contract ceiling reduced by 0.5 percentage point; a residency with exactly one returned payment has it reduced by 0.25 percentage point; a residency with two or more returned payments has no standing reduction.

## Questions and answers

**Q. What is counted?**
A. Returned payment entries posted on this residency's ledger — payments the bank returned unpaid — whose posting date falls within the 12 months ending on the day the increase is recorded.

**Q. Where does the 12-month window start?**
A. It ends on the day the increase is recorded and runs back 12 calendar months: for an increase recorded on January 15, 2027, a return posted on January 16, 2026 is inside the window and one posted on January 15, 2026 is outside it (hypothetical dates).

**Q. How large is each reduction?**

| Returned payments posted within the 12 months | Reduction of the contract ceiling percentage |
|---|---|
| None | 0.5 percentage point |
| Exactly one | 0.25 percentage point |
| Two or more | No standing reduction |

**Q. Is the reduction a share of the ceiling?**
A. No. It is a number of percentage points subtracted from the contract ceiling percentage.

**Q. Illustration?**
A. Hypothetically, a contract ceiling of 6.0 percent on a residency with exactly one returned payment in the 12 months becomes 5.75 percent after this reduction.
